options: User-visible symptoms, database execution signals, resource signals, configuration/state signals, external causation signals
CPU, memory, disk, network, storage

Application logs, database logs, OS logs, cloud logs, audit logs

questions.explain: The causal graph separates pre-seeded stable topology (physical dependency edges from engine knowledge) from live node state (real-time telemetry), so only the evidence layer changes during an incident.
options: To store historical incidents for reporting
To generate alert messages for PagerDuty
To schedule telemetry collection jobs
To separate stable, pre-seeded topology (physical dependencies from engine knowledge) from live node state (real-time telemetry), so only evidence changes during an incident

questions.explain: A match above 0.82 cosine similarity triggers HIGH_CONFIDENCE; 0.65-0.82 triggers MODERATE_CONFIDENCE; below 0.65 falls back to causal graph traversal.
options: Above 0.95 only
Above 0.50 triggers HIGH_CONFIDENCE
Above 0.82 triggers HIGH_CONFIDENCE; 0.65-0.82 is MODERATE; below 0.65 falls back to causal graph traversal
Any positive similarity triggers automatic remediation

questions.explain: The LLM layer runs asynchronously off the critical path for incidents the structured methods couldn't classify; the structured diagnosis runs synchronously in the same collection interval so autonomous low-risk actions never wait on a model API call.
options: The LLM runs first and gates all autonomous action
The LLM replaces the causal graph for known failures
The causal graph and signature matching run synchronously for fast-path response; the LLM runs asynchronously off the critical path for novel compound failures
The LLM output is passed directly to the executor without validation
questions.q: How is the LLM diagnosis layer positioned relative to the structured causal graph and signature matching, and why?

questions.explain: The schema enforces requires_human_approval per action: low-risk actions (killing an idle-in-transaction session, running ANALYZE, flushing a plan cache for one query) execute autonomously; above-threshold actions (failover, index creation on tables >50GB, parameter changes) queue for human approval with a 15-minute timeout.
options: Low-risk actions execute autonomously; high-risk actions (failover, index creation on tables >50GB, parameter changes) queue for human approval with a 15-minute timeout
All LLM-recommended actions require human approval
All LLM-recommended actions execute autonomously
The requires_human_approval flag is advisory only
